_comment: §27.2, §46.4, Appendix E.1). Read by BOTH sides so the credential DTO —
and above all its TIME UNIT — cannot drift apart again:
accepts this payload and reads the expiry as epoch MILLISECONDS;
`EphemeralCredential` serializes to exactly this shape, converting the
C1 REGRESSION GUARD. OpenAI returns `expires_at` as a 10-digit Unix epoch
SECONDS value. The webview compares expiry against Date.now(), which is
epoch MILLISECONDS. When Rust forwarded the raw seconds, every real
credential compared as already-expired (1785110400 < 1785110400000) and the
app rejected its own freshly minted secret before SDP negotiation — i.e. it
never transcribed at all in production. The unit is now in the field name.
provider timestamp. Do not replace it with a small synthetic number: a
millisecond-shaped fixture is exactly what hid this defect.
